themes.consensus_view: Banks agree AI borrowers now pay noticeably more to raise debt than everyone else and that the gap is likely to stick, but they split on whether that extra cost is fair payment for real growth or the first crack in the AI trade.

facts_agreed.claim: AI-linked borrowers are paying a wider borrowing cost than comparable non-AI companies, and that gap is expected to persist given how much money the buildout still needs.
evidence_quotes: our base case for the macro backdrop implies a healthy premium
AI-related issuance has been quite rate-insensitive given the existential rationale
wider spreads are becoming a less comfortable companion to equity gains

facts_agreed.claim: Bond investors are actively positioning against AI borrowers, and that pressure is now bleeding into how the equities trade.
evidence_quotes: All 10 of the most shorted bonds in IG are AI names
wider spreads are becoming a less comfortable companion to equity gains

facts_agreed.claim: AI spending is starting to show up in reported company results, which supports the case that the borrowers can carry the debt they are raising.
evidence_quotes: 25 companies in SPX are now quantifying the impact
latest earnings from CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer led to renewed optimism on the AI trade
The market is increasingly willing to give these businesses the benefit of the doubt

facts_contested.claim: whether the higher cost of AI debt reflects healthy funding of real growth or genuine credit deterioration
facts_contested.for_evidence: 25 companies in SPX are now quantifying the impact
facts_contested.against_evidence: All 10 of the most shorted bonds in IG are AI names

facts_contested.claim: whether the AI trade still has upside from here
facts_contested.for_evidence: latest earnings from CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer led to renewed optimism on the AI trade
facts_contested.against_evidence: the recent price action is beginning to challenge that view

themes.consensus_view: Three desks flag the upcoming US inflation reports as the week's main event and tie them to what the Fed does next, but none of them commits to a direction on the print.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks point to the upcoming US inflation reports as the near-term catalyst for this window.
JPMorgan links the July inflation report directly to what the market expects the Fed to do with rates.
evidence_quotes: July CPI print and Fed hike expectations

themes.consensus_view: Three desks keep the risk of oil tankers being blocked at the Strait of Hormuz on the watch list, but none of them has taken a side on whether it happens or what it does to prices.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks reference a possible closure or blockage of the Strait of Hormuz as a live risk this window without staking a directional view.
Mizuho EMEA extends the shipping-chokepoint watch beyond Hormuz to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

themes.consensus_view: Both banks expect memory chip prices to keep climbing into 2027 because supply stays short of demand, but they split on how much upside is left, with JPMorgan seeing the boom running through the end of 2028 and Goldman saying the easy gains from scarcity are already banked.

facts_agreed.claim: Memory supply stays short of demand and prices keep rising at least into 2027.
evidence_quotes: maintaining that the supply-demand shortage worsens into 2027E before a modest improvement in 2028E
Absolute prices should still rise into mid-2027, but the easy scarcity beta is behind us.

facts_contested.claim: how much of the memory upcycle is left after 2027
facts_contested.for_evidence: we continue to see the memory upcycle continuing through 28E-end
facts_contested.against_evidence: Absolute prices should still rise into mid-2027, but the easy scarcity beta is behind us.
